Part (i) is \cref{lem:target-contraction}. For (ii), take $c\le(2\attconst)^{-1/2}$:
\[
 \initscale^2\le c\mixrate\implies \attconst\initscale^4\le\attconst c^2\mixrate^2\le\tfrac{1}{2}\mixrate^2,
\]

bundle.leadIn: \paragraph{The network reads few letters at a time.} Scale every attention score by $\zeta\in[0,1]$ and expand in $\zeta$. At $\zeta=0$ attention is uniform and the MLPs are affine, so the network is additive over positions: each term reads at most one letter. Every interaction among letters passes through the scores, and a term with $k\ge1$ scores reads at most $2k+1$ letters and costs $\initscale^{2+4k}$ in the Jacobian (\cref{prop:score-degree}). Applying \cref{eq:credit-degree} term by term bounds the outcome credit. Call the credit of the score-dependent part $\mathbf J_{\mathrm{score}}$ of the Jacobian the \emph{score-mediated credit}: it contains every term that reads two or more letters, and also score-dependent terms that read one.

related.proof:
\emph{Ideal routing} ($\Omega_n=\infty$). With $m=\sum_tb_t$ and $[m=a]=\relu(m-a+1)-2\relu(m-a)+\relu(m-a-1)$,
\begin{gather*}
 \reg{match}_{1+t}=2\textstyle\sum_{a\in\Sigma}\relu\bigl([w_t=a]+[w^\star=a]-\frac{3}{2}\bigr)=b_t,\\
 \reg{prev}_{n+1+t}=\bm e_{s_{t-1}},\qquad \reg{mt}_{n+1+t}=b_t,\qquad
 \reg{cnt}_{n+3}=n\cdot\tfrac{1}{n}\textstyle\sum_tb_t=m,\qquad \reg{s0}_{n+3}=\bm e_{s_0},\\
 \reg{out}_{n+1+t}=\sum_{j,\iota}\bm e_{j+\iota}\,2\relu\Bigl([s_{t-1}=j]+[b_t=\iota]-\frac{3}{2}\Bigr)=\bm e_{s_t},\\
 \reg{out}_{n+3}=\sum_{j,a}\bm e_{j+a}[s_0=j][m=a]=\bm e_{s_n}.
\end{gather*}
The test $[s_0=j]$ is applied by adding $(n+2)([s_0=j]-1)$ to each of the three pre-activations of $[m=a]$. The readout has weight $20$
on $\reg{out}$ for value tokens and weight $20$ on the relevant $\reg{pos}$ coordinates for ``:'' and EOS; all unused maps are zero.

\emph{Finite scores.} A row puts total weight at most $\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n$ outside its sources, where
\[
 \omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n=(d_{\mathrm h}-1)e^{-\Omega_n}<\frac{2(n+3)}{(8(n+3))^3}=\frac{1}{256(n+3)^2}.
\]
Hence
\begin{gather*}
 |\reg{match}-b_t|\le2\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\qquad \|\reg{prev}-\bm e_{s_{t-1}}\|\le\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\qquad |\reg{mt}-b_t|\le3\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\\
 |\reg{cnt}-m|\le3n\,\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\qquad \|\reg{s0}-\bm e_{s_0}\|\le\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n .
\end{gather*}
At the step positions,
\[
 \mathrm{pre}_{s_t}\ge\tfrac{1}{2}-4\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n>0>\max_{a\ne s_t}\mathrm{pre}_a,\qquad \reg{out}_{s_t}\ge1-8\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n .
\]
At the answer position the errors add to $(4n+2)\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n<\frac{1}{192}$, and the three-ReLU test is $1$-Lipschitz, so
\[
 \reg{out}_{s_n}\ge1-(4n+2)\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\qquad \max_{a\ne s_n}\reg{out}_a\le(4n+2)\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n .
\]
With readout weight $20$ and $a^\star$ the gold token at a supervised position,
\[
 z_{a^\star}-\max_{a\ne a^\star}z_a\ge20\min\bigl\{1-8\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n,\ 1-2(4n+2)\omega^{\mathrm{leak}}_n\bigr\}>19 .
\]

\emph{Open neighbourhood.} Let $\mathcal P_n$ be the finite set of gold prefixes and supervised positions. By continuity there is
$r_{\mathrm{exec},n}>0$ with
\[
 \|\bm\theta-\bm\theta^\star\|<r_{\mathrm{exec},n}\implies\max_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\|\bm z_{\bm\theta}(P)-\bm z_{\bm\theta^\star}(P)\|_\infty<\tfrac{19}{2},
\]
so every greedy prediction is $a^\star$, and induction over the continuation gives the claim.

related.label: lem:target-contraction
related.title: Conditional contraction
related.proof:
Write $s_n=s_0+\sum_tb_t$. The letters are independent, so for $j\ne0$
\[
 \E\bigl[\alpha^{js_n}\bigm|\mathcal F_S\bigr]=\alpha^{js_0}\prod_{t\in S}\alpha^{jb_t}\prod_{t\notin S}\E\bigl[\alpha^{jb_t}\bigr]=\alpha^{js_0}\,\rho_j^{\,n-|S|}\prod_{t\in S}\alpha^{jb_t},
\]
whose modulus is $|\rho_j|^{n-|S|}$. Parseval over the nonconstant modes $j=1,\ldots,K-1$ gives the identity, and $|\rho_j|\le\mixrate$ the bound.
For a unit vector $\bm v$, $\mathbf H\bm v$ is $\mathcal F_S$-measurable, so
\begin{alignat*}{2}
 \bm v^\top\E[\mathbf H^\top\bm G]&=\E\bigl\langle\mathbf H\bm v,\ \E[\bm G\mid\mathcal F_S]\bigr\rangle &\qquad& \why{tower property}\\
 &\le\bigl(\E\|\mathbf H\bm v\|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\bigl(\E\|\E[\bm G\mid\mathcal F_S]\|^2\bigr)^{1/2} && \why{Cauchy--Schwarz}\\
 &\le\|\mathbf H\|_{L^2}\,\mixrate^{n-|S|} && \why{\cref{eq:horizon}}
\end{alignat*}
and the supremum over $\bm v$ is the claim.

related.label: lem:gradient-split
related.title: Gradient split
related.body:
\label{lem:gradient-split}
For every differentiable model, with $\outcredit(\bm\theta)=\E[\langle\bm z_{\bm\theta},\bm y-\bm u\rangle]$,
\[
 \nabla_{\bm\theta}\Lout=\underbrace{\E\bigl[(\Jz)^\top(\bm p-\bm u)\bigr]}_{\text{answer-independent}}-\underbrace{\nabla_{\bm\theta}\outcredit}_{\text{answer-dependent}},\qquad
 \nabla_{\bm\theta}\outcredit=\E\bigl[(\Jz)^\top(\bm y-\bm u)\bigr].
\]
related.proof: The logit gradient of the cross-entropy is $\bm p-\bm e_y=(\bm p-\bm u)-(\bm y-\bm u)$.

restatement.informalStatement:
Setting. Fix K ≥ 2, a finite alphabet Σ with a probability distribution μ on it, a query letter w* ∈ Σ with p := μ(w*) ∈ (0,1), a start count s0 ∈ Z_K and a horizon n ≥ 1 (n ≥ 2 in part (ii)). Letters w = (w_1,…,w_n) are i.i.d. μ; b_t = 1[w_t = w*]; the answer is s_n = s0 + Σ_t b_t (mod K); y = e_{s_n} ∈ R^K, u = (1/K)·1, G := y − u. All expectations E are over the letters only (s0 and w* fixed). λ := |1 − p + p·exp(2πi/K)| = max_{1≤j<K} |1 − p + p·exp(2πij/K)|, which lies in [0,1).

Part (i) (architecture-free). For every S ⊆ {1,…,n}, every finite index type ι, and every H : Σ^n → R^{K×ι} that depends only on (w_t)_{t∈S} (i.e. H(w) = H(w') whenever w_t = w'_t for all t ∈ S): ‖E[Hᵀ G]‖₂ ≤ λ^{n−|S|} · (E‖H‖_F²)^{1/2}. (Square-integrability is automatic for a finite alphabet.)

Part (ii). There exist constants c₀, c, C > 0 depending only on a0, c_emb, K and the number of heads per block (NOT on n, the widths d_res, d_h, w, the alphabet Σ, μ, p, s0, w*, the bias-norm bound N_b, the submasks, or ε) such that the following holds. Let θ̃ be any parameter vector of the two-block, no-LayerNorm, causal softmax-attention + ReLU-MLP Transformer of Assumption A1 (learned token and position embeddings, per-head W_Q, W_K ∈ R^{d_h×d_res}, W_V ∈ R^{d_res×d_res}, per-block MLP W_in ∈ R^{w×d_res}, b_in ∈ R^w, W_out ∈ R^{d_res×w}, readout V ∈ R^{K×d_res}; fixed nonempty causal per-head submasks allowed; relative position bias fixed at 0 and excluded from the parameters) such that every weight matrix and embedding block of θ̃ has operator norm ≤ a0, the value-token embeddings have smallest singular value ≥ c_emb > 0, every MLP bias coordinate satisfies |b̃_m| ≥ 1 and each MLP bias vector has Euclidean norm ≤ N_b. Let 0 < ε ≤ c₀·min(1, 1/N_b), θ0 := ε·θ̃, r0 := min(1/8, c_emb/4), and θ any parameter with ‖θ − θ0‖ ≤ r0·ε (Euclidean norm of the vectorized parameters, Frobenius per block). Let z_θ(w) ∈ R^K be the state (value-token) logits at the answer position (the ':' position n+3 of the prompt s0, w*, w_1,…,w_n, SEP, ':'), and z^{[0]}_θ(w) the same logits computed by the network in which every attention score in both blocks is multiplied by ζ = 0 (uniform attention over each head's visible set, composed through both blocks). Define the outcome credit OC(θ) := ‖∇_θ E[⟨z_θ, G⟩]‖ = ‖E[(∂z_θ/∂θ)ᵀ G]‖ and the score-mediated credit SC(θ) := ‖∇_θ E[⟨z_θ − z^{[0]}_θ, G⟩]‖ = ‖E[(∂z_θ/∂θ − ∂z^{[0]}_θ/∂θ)ᵀ G]‖. Then for every n ≥ 2:
  (ii-a) if ε² ≤ c·λ, then SC(θ) ≤ C·ε⁶·λ^{n−3} (an integer power; at n = 2 this is λ^{−1}, well defined because ε > 0 and ε² ≤ cλ force λ > 0);
  (ii-b) if ε ≤ c·λ, then OC(θ) ≤ C·ε·λ^n.

vocabulary.name: TaskParams / counting task
vocabulary.description: K ≥ 2 states Z_K; finite alphabet Σ with law μ (PMF); query letter w* with p = μ(w*) ∈ (0,1); start count s0 ∈ ZMod K (fixed); horizon n. Letters are i.i.d. μ. b_t = 1[w_t = w*], s_t = s_{t−1} + b_t mod K, answer s_n. Source: def:task (body.tex:78), ass:task (appendix.tex:55).
vocabulary.leanSketch:
structure Task where
  K : ℕ
  hK : 2 ≤ K
  Sym : Type
  [fin : Fintype Sym] [dec : DecidableEq Sym]
  μ : PMF Sym
  wstar : Sym
  s0 : ZMod K

def Task.p (T : Task) : ℝ := (T.μ T.wstar).toReal
def Task.answer (T : Task) {n} (w : Fin n → T.Sym) : ZMod T.K :=
  T.s0 + ∑ t, (if w t = T.wstar then 1 else 0)

vocabulary.name: letterLaw / expectation over letters
vocabulary.description: Product law of n i.i.d. letters; E[f] = Σ_{w : Fin n → Σ} (∏_t μ(w_t)) · f(w). Finite sum because Σ is finite; no measure theory needed.

vocabulary.name: targetSignal G = y − u
vocabulary.description: y = one-hot of the answer s_n in R^K, u = (1/K)·1; G(w) = y(w) − u. ‖G‖ ≤ 1.
vocabulary.leanSketch:
def G (T : Task) {n} (w : Fin n → T.Sym) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (ZMod T.K) :=
  fun a => (if a = T.answer w then 1 else 0) - 1 / T.K

vocabulary.name: mixrate λ
vocabulary.description: λ = |1 − p + p·e^{2πi/K}| (def:lambda, body.tex:89, eq:lambda). The paper also writes it as max_{1≤j<K}|ρ_j| with ρ_j = 1 − p + p α^j, α = e^{2πi/K}; equality of the two forms is a proof obligation (|ρ_j|² = 1 − 2p(1−p)(1 − cos(2πj/K))). 0 ≤ λ < 1 for K ≥ 2, p ∈ (0,1); λ = 0 is possible (K = 2, p = 1/2).
vocabulary.leanSketch:
noncomputable def mixrate (K : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ‖(1 - p : ℂ) + p * Complex.exp (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I / K)‖

vocabulary.name: dependsOnlyOn S
vocabulary.description: A function of the letters reads only the letters in S ⊆ Fin n: equal on letter sequences agreeing on S. Equivalent to F_S-measurability for finite Σ.
vocabulary.leanSketch:
def DependsOnlyOn {n α β} (S : Finset (Fin n)) (H : (Fin n → α) → β) : Prop :=
  ∀ w w', (∀ t ∈ S, w t = w' t) → H w = H w'

vocabulary.name: L2 norm of a matrix-valued feature
vocabulary.description: ‖H‖_{L²} = (E‖H‖_F²)^{1/2}; H has K rows and an arbitrary finite column index ι. E[Hᵀ G] ∈ R^ι with the Euclidean norm.
vocabulary.leanSketch:
def l2Norm (T : Task) {n ι} [Fintype ι] (H : (Fin n → T.Sym) → Matrix (ZMod T.K) ι ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (Ex T fun w => ∑ a, ∑ i, (H w a i)^2)

vocabulary.name: Arch (architecture shape)
vocabulary.description: Widths d_res, d_h, w (MLP), number of heads per block nH, two blocks, vocabulary = Σ ⊕ ZMod K ⊕ {SEP, ':', EOS}, sequence length L = n+4 for the outcome prompt, and a fixed per-(block, head, position i) visible set vis ⊆ {0,…,i}, nonempty (full prefix by default). Constants must not depend on any of these except nH.
vocabulary.leanSketch:
structure Arch (T : Task) (n : ℕ) where
  dres dh w nH : ℕ
  vis : Fin 2 → Fin nH → (i : Fin (n+4)) → Finset (Fin (n+4))
  vis_causal : ∀ l h i j, j ∈ vis l h i → j ≤ i
  vis_nonempty : ∀ l h i, (vis l h i).Nonempty

vocabulary.name: Params (θ, excluding the relative bias)
vocabulary.description: Token embedding E_tok : vocab → R^{d_res}, position embedding E_pos : Fin L → R^{d_res}; per block ℓ ∈ {1,2} and head h: W_Q, W_K : R^{d_h × d_res}, W_V : R^{d_res × d_res} (no separate output projection — follows the appendix display at appendix.tex:95); per block MLP W_in : R^{w×d_res}, b_in : R^w, W_out : R^{d_res×w} (no output bias); readout V : R^{K × d_res} (only the K value-token rows; other vocabulary rows never enter z). The relative bias β is fixed at 0 for this theorem and is omitted from θ (rem:norms, appendix.tex:76-81). Parameter space is a Euclidean space over the disjoint union of all block indices, so ‖θ‖ is the Euclidean norm of the vectorization (Frobenius per block).

vocabulary.name: forward (with score scale ζ)
vocabulary.description: x_i = E_tok(token_i) + E_pos(i). Block ℓ: ψ^{ℓ,h}_{ij} = (1/√d_h)(W_Q h_i)ᵀ(W_K h_j); ω_{i·} = softmax_{j ∈ vis(i)}(ζ ψ_{ij}); h_i ← h_i + Σ_h Σ_{j∈vis(i)} ω_{ij} W_V h_j; then h_i ← h_i + W_out ReLU(W_in h_i + b_in). Logits z = V h_{n+3}^{(2)} ∈ R^K. z_θ = forward ζ=1; z^{[0]}_θ = forward ζ=0 (block-2 residuals are those of the ζ=0 block-1 network: the composed network, not frozen scores; appendix.tex:298-306, direct_proofs/conditional_outcome.tex:29).

vocabulary.name: credit functionals
vocabulary.description: Φ_ξ(θ) = E⟨z_θ, ξ⟩, credit = ‖∇_θ Φ_ξ‖ = ‖E[(∂z_θ/∂θ)ᵀ ξ]‖ (def:credit, body.tex:165). Outcome credit: ξ = G. Score-mediated credit: ‖E[J_scoreᵀ G]‖ with J_score = ∂z_θ/∂θ − ∂z^{[0]}_θ/∂θ, equivalently ‖∇_θ E⟨z_θ − z^{[0]}_θ, G⟩‖ (appendix.tex:26-30).
vocabulary.leanSketch:
noncomputable def outcomeCredit A θ : ℝ :=
  ‖fderiv ℝ (fun θ' => Ex T fun w => inner (logits A 1 θ' w) (G T w)) θ‖
noncomputable def scoreCredit A θ : ℝ :=
  ‖fderiv ℝ (fun θ' => Ex T fun w => inner (logits A 1 θ' w - logits A 0 θ' w) (G T w)) θ‖

modelingChoices.item: Finite alphabet with a PMF; expectation as a finite weighted sum
modelingChoices.decision: Σ : Fintype, μ : PMF Σ; E f = Σ_w ∏_t μ(w_t) f(w)
modelingChoices.reason: Learned token embeddings presuppose a finite vocabulary; avoids measure theory and makes square-integrability trivial.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Part (i) is stated by the paper for general square-integrable H; on a finite space this is the full generality.

modelingChoices.item: 'depends only on letters in S' formalised as agreement on S implies equal values
modelingChoices.reason: Equivalent to F_S-measurability on a finite product space with full support; with zero-probability letters it is slightly stronger than a.s. measurability, which only weakens nothing in the conclusion (the hypothesis is stronger, theorem weaker by a null-set technicality).
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: If μ has zero-mass letters, the paper's F_S-measurable class is the same (σ-algebra measurability, not a.s.), so no gap.

modelingChoices.item: Credits defined via fderiv of the scalar credit functional
modelingChoices.decision: OC = ‖fderiv ℝ (θ ↦ E⟨z_θ, G⟩) θ‖, SC = ‖fderiv ℝ (θ ↦ E⟨z_θ − z^{[0]}_θ, G⟩) θ‖
modelingChoices.reason: Equals ‖E[Jᵀ G]‖ by linearity when z is differentiable; operator norm of a functional on EuclideanSpace equals the Euclidean norm of its gradient.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Mathlib's fderiv is 0 at non-differentiable points, which would make the bound vacuous there; a proof obligation must show differentiability on B_ε (fixed ReLU pattern) or the theorem should state DifferentiableAt as a conjunct so the bound is not trivially satisfied.

modelingChoices.reason: rem:norms: in thm:main β is fixed at 0 and excluded from θ and from the Jacobian.

modelingChoices.item: Readout restricted to K value-token rows; sequence truncated at n+4 positions
modelingChoices.reason: Other rows/positions have zero effect on z_θ (causality; z is the state logits).

modelingChoices.item: Single W_V per head (no output projection); score scale 1/√d_h; MLP without output bias
modelingChoices.reason: ass:arch does not pin these; the explicit display does, and prop:network's ε-power counting assumes them.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: A W_O would alter the power counting; handoff should note the chosen architecture.

modelingChoices.decision: Arch carries vis sets, required nonempty and ⊆ prefix; constants uniform in them
modelingChoices.reason: ass:arch allows submasks; thm:main uses only prop:network(i)-(iii), which hold with masks. Paper does not say masks are nonempty, but softmax over an empty set is undefined.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Could specialise to full prefix to simplify, at the cost of generality the paper claims; recommend keeping masks.

modelingChoices.item: Constants and the threshold c of ε0 are existential
modelingChoices.decision: ∀ a0 cemb K nH, ∃ c₀ c C > 0, ∀ n widths Σ μ masks θ̃ Nb ε θ, …
modelingChoices.reason: 'ε0 := c min(1, 1/N_b)' and the theorem's c, C are 'for suitable constants'. A single c vs separate c's are equivalent by taking minima.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Quantifier order must put the constants before n, widths, alphabet, p, N_b, masks; putting them after would make the theorem near-trivial.

modelingChoices.decision: Use zpow (λ ^ ((n:ℤ) − 3)) or the equivalent λ³·SC ≤ Cε⁶λ^n
modelingChoices.reason: Negative exponent at n = 2; λ > 0 follows from ε > 0 and ε² ≤ cλ.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: With ℕ subtraction n − 3 = 0 at n = 2, the bound would become Cε⁶, which is a different (stronger) claim — must not be used.

modelingChoices.decision: s0@0, w*@1, w_t@(1+t), SEP@(n+2), ':'@(n+3); answer logits at n+3
modelingChoices.reason: appendix.tex:107-115. The proof only uses that non-letter tokens are fixed and the answer position is fixed.

modelingChoices.decision: Prove the activation pattern is constant on a neighbourhood of every θ ∈ B_ε (the paper proves it on the doubled ball), so z is smooth there
modelingChoices.reason: Needed for fderiv to be the real Jacobian.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: If closedBall boundary points were not interior to a constant-pattern region, fderiv could be 0 there; the doubled-ball claim (appendix.tex:229-230) covers it.

program: Define the deterministic forward map logits (A : Arch) (ζ : ℝ) (θ : Params A) (w : Fin n → Σ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (ZMod K) for the two-block, no-LayerNorm, causal softmax Transformer with per-head W_Q, W_K (d_h×d_res), W_V (d_res×d_res), scores (1/√d_h)⟨W_Q h_i, W_K h_j⟩ scaled by ζ, softmax over a fixed nonempty causal visible set, residual ReLU MLP W_out ReLU(W_in h + b_in), readout V (K×d_res), evaluated at position n+3 of the outcome prompt.
ζ must scale the scores in both blocks inside the composed computation (block-2 scores computed from the ζ-network's block-1 residuals).
No relative bias; Params is a EuclideanSpace over a Fintype index so ‖·‖ is the vectorized Euclidean norm.
Task: Fintype alphabet, PMF μ, query w*, s0 : ZMod K; answer = s0 + #{t : w_t = w*} mod K; G = onehot(answer) − (1/K)1; expectation = finite weighted sum.
pseudocode: May present the forward pass with ζ hidden (ζ = 1) and z^{[0]} as 'uniform attention'; must state that z^{[0]} is the composed ζ = 0 network.
May present masks as 'full prefix by default'.
theorem: One theorem with two parts (or two theorems sharing the setting): part (i) architecture-free: ∀ S H, DependsOnlyOn S H → ‖Ex (fun w => (H w)ᵀ *ᵥ G w)‖ ≤ mixrate K p ^ (n − S.card) * l2Norm H.

Part (ii): ∀ a0 cemb (K) nH, ∃ c₀ c C > 0, ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ Task with that K and p ∈ (0,1), ∀ Arch with nH heads (any widths, masks), ∀ θ̃ Nb with InitHyp θ̃ a0 cemb Nb, ∀ ε, 0 < ε → ε ≤ c₀ * min 1 (1/Nb) → ∀ θ ∈ closedBall (ε • θ̃) (min (1/8) (cemb/4) * ε) → (ε^2 ≤ c * λ → scoreCredit θ ≤ C * ε^6 * λ ^ ((n:ℤ) − 3)) ∧ (ε ≤ c * λ → outcomeCredit θ ≤ C * ε * λ ^ n).
Constants must be quantified before n, widths, alphabet, μ, p, s0, w*, Nb, masks, θ̃, ε, θ.
Do not use ℕ subtraction for n − 3. Optionally add DifferentiableAt conjuncts so the fderiv bound is not vacuous.
handoff: Check quantifier order of constants (uniform in n, widths, N_b, p, alphabet).
Check λ is |1 − p + p e^{2πi/K}| and the exponent n − 3 is an integer power.
Check z^{[0]} is the ζ = 0 composed network, and that both credits exclude β.
Check part (i) uses the Euclidean norm on E[Hᵀ G] and the Frobenius L² norm on H.
Report that ε > 0 was added (implicit in the paper) and that eq:thm1-full's |Φ_out| bound is a non-goal.

headline.shape: Deterministic inequality theorem (no algorithm, no probability monad): (i) ∀ S-local H, ‖E[Hᵀ(y−u)]‖ ≤ λ^{n−|S|}‖H‖_{L²}; (ii) ∃ c₀ c C > 0 uniform in n/widths/alphabet such that ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ admissible θ̃, ε ∈ (0, c₀ min(1,1/N_b)], θ ∈ B_ε: ε² ≤ cλ → scoreCredit ≤ Cε⁶λ^{n−3}, and ε ≤ cλ → outcomeCredit ≤ Cελ^n. Expectations are finite sums over the letter law.

ambiguities: ε > 0 is not stated in thm:main (lem:score-sum assumes it). At ε = 0, θ0 = 0, all MLP pre-activations are exactly 0 and the ReLU is not differentiable; add 0 < ε.

λ can be 0 (K = 2, p = 1/2) and at n = 2 the bound uses λ^{−1}. With ε > 0 the hypothesis ε² ≤ cλ forces λ > 0, so the statement is well defined once ε > 0 is added; Lean must use an integer power, not ℕ subtraction.

Quantifier order / dependence of constants: the paper says c, C depend only on a0, c_emb, K and the number of blocks and heads; the c inside ε0 = c min(1,1/N_b) is also an existential constant. The Lean statement must fix these before n, widths, N_b, alphabet, p.

Architecture details not pinned in ass:arch: whether heads have an output projection W_O, whether scores carry 1/√d_h, whether MLPs have an output bias. The appendix display (appendix.tex:95-96) fixes: no W_O, 1/√d_h, no output bias. Adopted.

'Every weight matrix and embedding block … operator norm ≤ a0': unclear whether the readout V counts as a weight matrix (assumed yes) and how embedding blocks are shaped (token embedding as d_res×|vocab|, position embedding as d_res×L, assumed).

z^{[0]} / J^{[0]}: defined by multiplying every score by ζ in both blocks of the composed network; J^{[0]} = ∂_θ z(0). The body paragraph is informal; appendix eq:score-split and direct_proofs/conditional_outcome.tex:29 fix the composed reading.
Part (i) norm conventions: E[Hᵀ G] uses the Euclidean norm, ‖H‖_{L²} uses Frobenius (lem:target-contraction). H has K rows and arbitrary column count.
The alphabet is never stated to be finite; finiteness is assumed (learned token embeddings).
Submasks are allowed by ass:arch but their visible sets are not required to be nonempty; we require nonempty.
Differentiability: the credit is a gradient; the theorem implicitly needs z_θ differentiable at θ ∈ B_ε (fixed ReLU pattern on the doubled ball, appendix.tex:229-230).

Constants c₀ (in ε0), c, C existential, chosen after a0, c_emb, K, nH and before everything else.
Architecture fixed per appendix.tex:95-96: single W_V per head (d_res×d_res), 1/√d_h score scaling, MLP with input bias only, no LayerNorm, readout V : K×d_res, β omitted.
ReLU pattern is constant on a neighbourhood of B_ε for all inputs and all ζ ∈ [0,1] (|b_m| ≥ (3/4)ε > Cε² ≥ |(W_in h)_m|), hence z is differentiable and fderiv is the Jacobian.
max_{1≤j<K} |1 − p + p α^j| = |1 − p + p α| (|ρ_j|² = 1 − 2p(1−p)(1 − cos 2πj/K)); needed for |ρ_j| ≤ λ in part (i).

prop:score-degree / prop:network are the bulk of part (ii) (ζ-Taylor expansion, letter-support counting ≤ 2k+1, absolute-sum bounds Cε²(C_att ε⁴)^k uniform in n and widths). These are same-paper lemmas, not priors.
The fderiv-based credit is vacuously small at non-differentiable points; handoff must confirm differentiability is proved (or stated) so the bound is not trivially satisfied.
Finite alphabet and finite-sum expectation; square-integrability dropped as automatic.

Constant independence from p and the alphabet is not listed explicitly in the paper's constant list but follows from it (constants depend only on a0, c_emb, K, blocks, heads); handoff should confirm the Lean constants are not allowed to depend on p, μ, Σ, N_b or widths.

callerConditions.name: derive_Catt_eps4_le_half_lambdaSq
callerConditions.condition: C_att · ε⁴ ≤ (1/2)·λ², to be derived (not assumed) from ε² ≤ c·λ by fixing the existential constant c := (2·C_att)⁻¹ᐟ² (or any 0 < c ≤ (2·C_att)⁻¹ᐟ²) before lem:score-sum's internal hypothesis is invoked.
callerConditions.source: Paper/appendix.tex:530-532 ('For (ii), take c ≤ (2C_att)^{-1/2}: ε²≤cλ ⟹ C_attε⁴ ≤ C_att c²λ² ≤ (1/2)λ²')
callerConditions.leanBinder: have hc : C_att * ε^4 ≤ (1/2) * λ^2 := by have := hε2 -- ε^2 ≤ c*λ with c chosen as (2*Catt)⁻¹ᐟ²; nlinarith/field_simp from that choice
callerConditions.whyNeeded: lem:score-sum's hypothesis is exactly 'C_att ε⁴ ≤ λ²/2'; the headline's hypothesis is 'ε² ≤ cλ'. The bridge is a specific algebraic choice of c tied to C_att (itself a constant produced by prop:score-degree, not independently chosen). If the Lean assembly treats c as free rather than defined via C_att, the invocation of lem:score-sum cannot be discharged.

callerConditions.name: derive_lambda_pos_from_eps_pos_and_eps2_le_c_lambda
callerConditions.condition: 0 < λ, derived from 0 < ε, c > 0 and ε² ≤ c·λ (so c·λ ≥ ε² > 0, hence λ > 0 since c > 0).
callerConditions.source: Paper/appendix.tex:494-496 (lem:score-sum assumes '0<λ<1'); ambiguity note on λ=0 at K=2,p=1/2 and the λ^{n-3} zpow at n=2
callerConditions.leanBinder: have hλpos : 0 < λ := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg ε, hεpos, hc_pos, h_eps2_le_cλ]
callerConditions.whyNeeded: lem:score-sum's standing hypothesis is '0<λ<1', but the headline's ambient hypotheses (K≥2, p∈(0,1)) only give λ<1, not λ>0 (λ=0 is reachable at K=2,p=1/2). Without this derivation step, invoking lem:score-sum is unjustified, and λ^((n:ℤ)-3) at n=2 (a zpow with exponent -1) is ill-defined/wrong at λ=0 (Mathlib convention 0⁻¹=0 would make the RHS 0, forcing scoreCredit=0, which is not what is proved).

callerConditions.name: lambda_lt_one_standing_fact
callerConditions.condition: λ < 1, derivable once from K ≥ 2 and p ∈ (0,1) alone (no dependence on ε or θ).
callerConditions.leanBinder: theorem mixrate_lt_one (hK : 2 ≤ K) (hp : p ∈ Set.Ioo (0:ℝ) 1) : mixrate K p < 1
callerConditions.whyNeeded: Both lem:target-contraction and lem:score-sum require λ<1 as a standing precondition; it should be proved once from the Task-level hypotheses rather than re-derived ad hoc at each call site, and the cross-check belongs in ProblemSetting per the audit-surface discipline.

callerConditions.name: visible_set_nonempty_before_softmax
callerConditions.condition: ∀ block l, head h, position i: (vis l h i).Nonempty, must hold before the forward pass computes softmax at (l,h,i).
callerConditions.source: Paper/ass:arch appendix.tex:34-41 ('A head may have a fixed, input-independent causal submask')
callerConditions.leanBinder: already a structure field `vis_nonempty : ∀ l h i, (vis l h i).Nonempty`; must actually be consumed as a side condition at every softmax call site in the forward-pass definition, not merely declared
callerConditions.whyNeeded: Softmax over an empty visible set is mathematically undefined (0/0); the paper never states masks are nonempty but silently assumes it. route.why: No library proves any of the three parts. Part (i) is a short finite-sum argument: a resampling identity, Fourier analysis on ZMod K, then Cauchy–Schwarz. sourceTheorems.statement: DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x → f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f → DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f₁ x
sourceTheorems.why: Proves the DifferentiableAt conjuncts. On the doubled ball the ReLU equals a fixed 0/1 mask (pattern lemma), so each functional agrees near θ with a max-free expression made of exp, division by positive sums, and polynomial operations.

sourceTheorems.statement: DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x → DifferentiableAt 𝕜 g x → fderiv 𝕜 (fun y => f y + g y) x = fderiv 𝕜 f x + fderiv 𝕜 g x
sourceTheorems.why: (ii-b) splits outcomeFunctional = zeroOrderFunctional + scoreFunctional and reuses (ii-a).

sourceTheorems.statement: 0 < ε → Metric.ball x ε ∈ 𝓝 x
sourceTheorems.why: Supplies the `∀ᶠ θ' in 𝓝 θ` in norm_fderiv_le_of_lip'. Use ball(θ, r₀ε) ⊆ closedBall(εθ̃, 2r₀ε), the doubled ball.

sourceTheorems.why: Product form of the letter law. It gives Σ_w letterWeight w = 1 and E[χ_j(count over Sᶜ)] = ρ_j^{|Sᶜ|} (independence, used in the forward direction).

sourceTheorems.why: Finite (series-free) proof of the locality-norm exponential bound N(e^f − 1) ≤ e^{N f} − 1, via e^{Σ_S T_S} = Π_S(1 + (e^{T_S} − 1)).

sourceTheorems.statement: (e : α ≃ β) (f : β → M) : ∑ x, f (e x) = ∑ y, f y
sourceTheorems.why: The resampling involution (w,v) ↦ (merge w v, merge v w) on (Fin n → Sym)², which proves E[HᵀG] = E[HᵀĜ] with no subtype equivalences.

sourceTheorems.name: Real.cos_le_cos_of_nonneg_of_le_pi
sourceTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ x → y ≤ π → x ≤ y → cos y ≤ cos x

sourceTheorems.name: ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm / opNorm_le_bound
sourceTheorems.why: Unpacks `Trace.opNorm` (a CLM norm of Matrix.toEuclideanLin) into ‖M x‖₂ ≤ opNorm M ‖x‖₂. Also gives opNorm ≤ Frobenius ≤ the full parameter norm.

sourceTheorems.name: Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq / inner_mul_le_norm_mul_norm
sourceTheorems.why: Cauchy–Schwarz in part (i) (‖Hᵀg‖ ≤ ‖H‖_F‖g‖, and Jensen Σπ‖H‖_F ≤ (Σπ‖H‖_F²)^{1/2}) and in the locality credit lemma.

proofSteps.step: 0. Before anything else, open Trace/Model/Prior.lean and record what `Trace.Prior` asserts. Do not add to it. If it is a hypothesis the route below never uses, ignore it (`_hprior`). If it is strong or vacuous (e.g. implies False), report that immediately as a statement defect: every surface theorem is then conditional on it.
proofSteps.why: The fixed surface threads `hprior` through all three theorems. Its content decides whether part (ii) can shortcut through a stated prop:score-degree.

proofSteps.step: 1a. Part (i), resampling identity. Define merge S w v t := if t ∈ S then w t else v t and Ĝ(w) := Σ_v letterWeight v • targetSignal (merge S w v). Prove Ex (fun w => (H w)ᵀ *ᵥ G w) = Ex (fun w => (H w)ᵀ *ᵥ Ĝ w). Insert Σ_v letterWeight v = 1, then reindex by the involution e(w,v) = (merge S w v, merge S v w). It preserves letterWeight w * letterWeight v (the products split over S and Sᶜ), and H w = H (merge S w v) by hH.
proofSteps.tacticShape: rw [← mul_one (Ex …), ← sum_letterWeight_eq_one]; simp only [Ex, Finset.sum_mul, Finset.smul_sum]; rw [← Fintype.sum_prod_type']; exact (Equiv.sum_comp eInvol _).symm ▸ …   (eInvol built with `Function.Involutive.toPerm`)
proofSteps.why: This is the finite-sum form of the tower property. It avoids Equiv.piEquivPiSubtypeProd and any conditional-expectation API.

proofSteps.step: 1b. Part (i), Fourier form of Ĝ. For j : ZMod K, Σ_a Ĝ(w)_a · χ(j·a) = (if j = 0 then 0 else χ(j·(s0 + c_S(w))) · ρ_j^{|Sᶜ|}), where χ = ZMod.stdAddChar, ρ_j = (1−p) + p·χ(j) and c_S(w) = Σ_{t∈S}[w t = w⋆]. Proof: χ is additive, and Σ_v Π_t f_t(v t) = Π_t Σ_x f_t(x) (Fintype.prod_sum) with f_t = μ for t ∈ S. The j = 0 case is Σ_a q(a) − K·(1/K) = 0.
proofSteps.tacticShape: simp only [Ĝ, targetSignal, answer, AddChar.map_add_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum]; rw [Fintype.prod_sum]; split_ifs; ring_nf; field_simp
proofSteps.why: Independence of the letters. This is the only place the product law matters.

proofSteps.step: 1c. Part (i), Parseval on ZMod K. For f : ZMod K → ℂ: Σ_a ‖f a‖² = (1/K) Σ_j ‖Σ_a f a · χ(j·a)‖². Prove it from character orthogonality (AddChar.sum_mulShift with ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar), expanding |·|² = z·conj z. Then ‖Ĝ(w)‖₂² = (1/K) Σ_{j≠0} |ρ_j|^{2|Sᶜ|} ≤ λ^{2(n−|S|)}, using |ρ_j| ≤ λ (step 1d), the K−1 nonzero modes, and (K−1)/K ≤ 1.
proofSteps.tacticShape: own lemma `parseval_zmod`: simp only [Complex.sq_norm/normSq, map_sum, Finset.sum_comm, ← AddChar.map_neg_eq_conj]; rw [AddChar.sum_mulShift]; simp [Finset.sum_ite_eq]
proofSteps.why: This is eq:horizon (appendix.tex:267). Check first whether Mathlib already has a ZMod.dft Parseval (grep `dft` in Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/ZMod.lean). If so, use it.

proofSteps.step: 1d. |ρ_j| ≤ mixrate K p for j ≠ 0. Use |(1−p) + p z|² = (1−p)² + p² + 2p(1−p)·Re z for |z| = 1, with Re χ(j) = cos(2π j.val/K) ≤ cos(2π/K). Also prove 0 ≤ mixrate ≤ 1 (triangle inequality), needed downstream.
proofSteps.tacticShape: rw [← sq_le_sq₀ …, Complex.sq_abs, Complex.normSq_apply]; simp [stdAddChar_apply, Complex.exp_re]; nlinarith [Real.cos_le_cos_of_nonneg_of_le_pi …, cos_two_pi_sub …]
proofSteps.why: The paper's λ = max_j|ρ_j| is a proof obligation; the surface defines λ = |ρ_1|.

proofSteps.step: 1e. Close part (i). ‖Ex(Hᵀ Ĝ)‖ ≤ Σ_w π(w)‖H w‖_F‖Ĝ w‖ ≤ λ^{n−|S|} Σ_w π(w)‖H w‖_F ≤ λ^{n−|S|}·sqrt(Σ_w π(w)‖H w‖_F²) = λ^{n−|S|}·l2Norm H. Note |Sᶜ| = n − S.card via Finset.card_compl and Fintype.card_fin, so ℕ subtraction is harmless here.
proofSteps.tacticShape: calc featureCredit T H = ‖toLp (Ex (Hᵀ Ĝ))‖ := by rw [resample] _ ≤ … := norm_sum_le … _ ≤ … := gcongr … _ ≤ … := Real.le_sqrt … (Cauchy–Schwarz with Σπ = 1)
proofSteps.why: Delivers `Trace.Proof.unseenLettersContraction`. Uses K ≥ 1 only; hK, hp0 and hp1 are unused.

proofSteps.step: 2. Locality calculus (proof-side file Trace/Analysis/Locality.lean). For a normed space E and κ ∈ (0,1], let a decomposition be T : Finset (Fin n) → ((Fin n → Sym) → E) with DependsOn (T S) S and f = Σ_S T S. Grouping terms by support set loses nothing. Define locNorm κ f := sInf {Σ_S κ⁻¹^{S.card}·‖T S‖_sup}. Lemmas: ‖f‖_sup ≤ locNorm ≤ κ^{-n}‖f‖_sup; triangle; scalar; constants (S = ∅); `DependsOn f S → locNorm ≤ κ^{-|S|}‖f‖`; bilinear bound locNorm(B f g) ≤ ‖B‖·locNorm f·locNorm g (regroup S ∪ S', using κ^{-|S∪S'|} ≤ κ^{-|S|}κ^{-|S'|}); exp bound locNorm(exp∘f − 1) ≤ exp(locNorm f) − 1 (finite product expansion, Finset.prod_add); inverse bound locNorm((1+β)⁻¹ − 1) ≤ N/(1−N) for N = locNorm β < 1 (Neumann series plus the sup-norm comparison to pass to the limit); softmax lemma: if max_{j∈V} locNorm ψ_j ≤ M ≤ 1/4 then Σ_{j∈V} locNorm(softmax_V(ψ)_j − 1/|V|) ≤ 8M, plus its two-point version Σ_j locNorm(ω_j(ψ') − ω_j(ψ)) ≤ C·max_j locNorm(ψ'_j − ψ_j).
proofSteps.tacticShape: a series of 15-40 line lemmas; `le_csInf`/`csInf_le` or a predicate `LocBound κ f B` with existential decompositions to avoid sInf bookkeeping
proofSteps.why: This replaces the paper's 'term T_{k,ν} reads ≤ 2k+1 letters, Σ_ν sup‖T‖ ≤ …' enumeration with a submultiplicative seminorm. The softmax lemma is uniform in |V|, which gives uniformity in n.

proofSteps.step: 3. Locality credit lemma: for f : (Fin n → Sym) → (ZMod K → ℝ) and λ = mixrate K T.p > 0, |Ex (fun w => f w ⬝ᵥ targetSignal w)| ≤ √K · λ^n · locNorm λ f. Apply part (i) with ι = Unit to each T S (H w = column T S w), use l2Norm ≤ sup and the Euclidean-vs-sup factor √K, then use λ^{n−|S|} = λ^n·λ^{-|S|}.
proofSteps.tacticShape: obtain ⟨T, hdep, rfl, hB⟩; simp only [Ex, dotProduct_sum…]; refine (abs_sum_le_sum_abs …).trans ?_; gcongr with S; have := Trace.Proof.unseenLettersContraction hprior hK T hp0 hp1 n S (H := fun w => Matrix.of fun a _ => T S w a) …
proofSteps.why: This is how part (ii) consumes part (i). It is the formal version of 'apply lem:target-contraction term by term'.

proofSteps.step: 4. Parameter bounds on the doubled ball D := closedBall(εθ̃, 2r₀ε) with 2r₀ ≤ 1/4. For θ' ∈ D: every accessor block has opNorm ≤ a₁ε with a₁ := max a0 0 + 1/4 (perturbation: opNorm ≤ Frobenius ≤ ‖θ'−εθ̃‖); for θ, θ' ∈ D the block differences have opNorm ≤ ‖θ'−θ‖; embedding columns have Euclidean norm ≤ a₁ε; |bIn l m| ≥ (3/4)ε and sign(bIn l m) = sign(θ̃.bIn l m); ‖bIn l‖ ≤ ε(Nb + 1/4).
proofSteps.tacticShape: generic lemma: for an injective index map g into ParamIdx, Σ_i θ (g i)^2 ≤ ‖θ‖^2 (Finset.sum_map + sum_le_univ_sum_of_nonneg); then one lemma per accessor via Sum.inl_injective/Sum.inr_injective
proofSteps.why: Every ε power in the analysis comes from here. Only r₀ ≤ 1/8 is used; cemb enters only through r₀.

proofSteps.step: 5. Pattern lemma, the coupling to a ReLU-free network. For θ' ∈ D, every w, every real ζ, l ∈ {0,1}, position i and unit m: max(pre,0) = (if 0 < θt.bIn l m then pre else 0), where pre = (wIn l *ᵥ a_i) m + bIn l m. Proof: attention weights are convex for any ζ, so the sup bounds ‖x_i‖ ≤ 2a₁ε, ‖a_i‖ ≤ Cε and ‖block-1 output‖ ≤ Cε use ε·Nb ≤ c₀. Then |(wIn a)_m| ≤ Cε² < (3/4)ε ≤ |b_m| once c₀ is small. Then prove DifferentiableAt of logits A ζ · w at θ (ζ ∈ {0,1}) through the max-free form plus congr_of_eventuallyEq, and lift to the two functionals by DifferentiableAt.sum/mul.
proofSteps.tacticShape: lemma relu_eq_mask …; DifferentiableAt: `refine (hLin).congr_of_eventuallyEq (Filter.eventually_of_mem (Metric.ball_mem_nhds θ hr) fun θ' h => …)`; hLin by `fun_prop` plus DifferentiableAt.div with `Finset.sum_pos (fun _ _ => Real.exp_pos _) (A.vis_nonempty …)`
proofSteps.why: Discharges both DifferentiableAt conjuncts and makes the MLPs exactly affine (W_out·D·(W_in a + b)) on D, as the paper assumes.

proofSteps.step: 6. Network propagation (Trace/Analysis/NetworkBounds.lean), all with κ ∈ (0,1], hypothesis ε² ≤ c·κ, θ, θ' ∈ D and ρ := ‖θ'−θ‖/ε. Bound locNorm κ of: (value) embed ≤ Cεκ^{-1} (≤ Cε at the answer position); scores ψ ≤ Cε⁴κ^{-2}; block outputs ≤ Cεκ^{-1}, and ≤ Cε + Cε²κ^{-1} at position n+3; logits ≤ C(ε² + ε³κ^{-1}). (ζ-difference, ζ=1 minus ζ=0) attention weights Σ_j ≤ Cε⁴κ^{-2}; block-1 output ≤ Cε⁶κ^{-3}; logits ≤ Cε⁷κ^{-3}. (θ-difference) each of the above times Cρ. (mixed) logits ≤ Cρε⁷κ^{-3}. Use ω(ζ=0) = 1/|vis|, which is θ-independent, so the mixed difference of the weights is just the θ-difference of ω(1). Every C depends only on a0, K, nH.
proofSteps.tacticShape: one lemma per layer and per difference type (≈16 lemmas), each a `calc` chaining the bilinear bound, the softmax lemma and step-4 bounds; finish with `nlinarith`/`gcongr`, or `positivity` for side conditions
proofSteps.why: This is the bulk. It reproduces the paper's power counting (score ε⁴λ^{-2}, value path ε²λ^{-1}) without the k-indexed expansion or the remainder J_rem.

proofSteps.step: 7. Close (ii-a) (`Trace.Proof.unseenLettersScoreCredit`). Choose c₀, c, C from a0 and nH (and K, through √K) explicitly. Given the hypotheses, λ > 0 follows from ε > 0 and ε² ≤ cλ. For θ' ∈ ball(θ, r₀ε) ⊆ D: scoreFunctional θ' − scoreFunctional θ = Ex(⟨Δ_θΔ_ζ z, G⟩), which is ≤ √K λ^n·Cρε⁷λ^{-3} = C'ε⁶λ^{(n:ℤ)−3}‖θ'−θ‖. Apply norm_fderiv_le_of_lip'. DifferentiableAt comes from step 5.
proofSteps.tacticShape: refine ⟨c₀, c, C, …, fun n hn Sym _ _ T hp0 hp1 A θt Nb hI ε hε hε0 θ hθ hc => ⟨diff_score …, ?_⟩⟩; exact norm_fderiv_le_of_lip' (by positivity) (Filter.eventually_of_mem (Metric.ball_mem_nhds _ _) fun θ' h => by rw [zpow_sub₀ hλ.ne', zpow_natCast]; …)
proofSteps.why: Uses credit lemma (step 3) with κ = λ and the mixed bound of step 6.

proofSteps.step: 8. Close (ii-b) (`Trace.Proof.unseenLettersOutcomeCredit`). Get (c₀', c', C') from the score owner. Set c := min c' 1 (and c ≤ 1), so ε ≤ cλ gives ε ≤ λ ≤ 1 and ε² ≤ c'λ. Split outcomeFunctional = zeroOrderFunctional + scoreFunctional, where zeroOrderFunctional θ = Ex⟨logits A 0 θ w, G⟩ (Finset.sum_add_distrib, add_dotProduct). The fderiv of zeroOrderFunctional is bounded by the step-3/step-6 θ-difference bound at ζ = 0: √K λ^n·Cρ(ε² + ε³λ^{-1}) ≤ C''ελ^n‖θ'−θ‖. The score part satisfies C'ε⁶λ^{n−3} ≤ C'ελ^n because ε⁵ ≤ λ³. Combine with fderiv_add and norm_add_le.
proofSteps.tacticShape: obtain ⟨c₀', c', C', …, hS⟩ := Trace.Proof.unseenLettersScoreCredit hprior a0 cemb hcemb K hK nH; refine ⟨min c₀' c₀'', min c' (min 1 c''), …⟩; rw [outcome_eq_add, fderiv_add hd0 hdS]; exact (norm_add_le _ _).trans (add_le_add h0 hS') |>.trans (by nlinarith …)
proofSteps.why: This is lem:score-sum's 'adding the zero-order term'. Reusing (ii-a) avoids a second ζ-difference analysis.

proofSteps.step: 9. Discharge the surface: replace each `sorry` in Trace/Model/Theorem.lean with `:= Trace.Proof.<owner> hprior …`. Theorem.lean imports the three Analysis files; that is allowed, since Theorem is the assembly file. The capstone is already `⟨…, …, …⟩`. Run `#print axioms Trace.unseen_letters_erase_outcome_credit` and `#modelClosureOfType`.
proofSteps.tacticShape: theorem unseen_letters_contraction … := Trace.Proof.unseenLettersContraction hprior hK T hp0 hp1 n S H hH
proofSteps.why: Keeps the statement fixed and puts the proof content outside Model/.

statementRisks.risk: `hprior : Trace.Prior` may make the whole theorem conditional, or vacuous if Prior is unsatisfiable. That would be invisible in the headline's binder list.
statementRisks.check: Print `Trace.Prior`. If the route never uses it, say so in the handoff and suggest dropping it from the surface in a later pass. If it states a paper lemma, record exactly which one and treat the result as conditional on it.

statementRisks.risk: ℕ subtraction in λ^{n−3} would silently strengthen (ii-a) to Cε⁶ at n = 2, 3.
statementRisks.check: The surface correctly uses `mixrate K T.p ^ ((n : ℤ) - 3)` (zpow). Keep it. Proofs need `zpow_sub₀` with λ ≠ 0, which follows from ε > 0 and ε² ≤ cλ.

statementRisks.risk: Constants quantified in the wrong order (after n, the widths, Nb, the alphabet or p) would trivialize part (ii).
statementRisks.check: The surface puts ∃ c₀ c C right after a0, cemb, K, nH. In the proof, define the constants explicitly from a0, nH and K before `intro n`. Never use n, A.dres, A.dh, A.dmlp, Fintype.card Sym, Nb or T.p in them.

statementRisks.risk: fderiv is 0 at non-differentiable points, so a credit bound could hold vacuously.
statementRisks.check: The DifferentiableAt conjuncts are present. Prove them from the pattern lemma (step 5), not from the Lipschitz bound.

statementRisks.risk: Width-dependent constants can creep in through the Pi sup norm: residual vectors are typed `Fin A.dres → ℝ`, whose Mathlib norm is the sup norm, while `Trace.opNorm` is Euclidean.
statementRisks.check: In every locality and sup bound, measure residual vectors in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin dres) via `WithLp.toLp 2`. Grep the proof files for norms of bare `Fin _ → ℝ` vectors. √K factors (logits) are allowed; √dres factors are not.

statementRisks.risk: Part (i) needs λ^{n−|S|} with |Sᶜ| = n − S.card. A mismatch between `Finset.card_compl` and ℕ subtraction could look like an off-by-something.
statementRisks.check: S.card ≤ n by Finset.card_le_univ and Fintype.card_fin, so the ℕ subtraction is exact. Prove `(Sᶜ).card = n - S.card` once and rewrite with it.

statementRisks.risk: Degenerate Nb (dmlp = 0 allows any Nb, including Nb ≤ 0) makes `min 1 (1/Nb)` ≤ 0.
statementRisks.check: The hypothesis ε ≤ c₀·min 1 (1/Nb) with ε > 0 then has no solutions, so the theorem is vacuous there, not false. Do not add Nb > 0. When Nb > 0, the proof uses ε·Nb ≤ c₀ (from ε ≤ c₀/Nb) and ε ≤ c₀.

statementRisks.risk: Paper gaps the formalization will hit: (1) ε > 0 missing in thm:main (already repaired); (2) λ = 0 is possible (K = 2, p = 1/2), but ε² ≤ cλ with ε > 0 excludes it; (3) the restriction n ≥ 2 is not needed by this route.
statementRisks.check: Keep the surface as-is. In the handoff, report that the proof never uses `2 ≤ n` (hn is unused), which is evidence that the paper's restriction is an artifact of k₀ = ⌈(n−1)/2⌉ in lem:score-sum.

statementRisks.risk: Part (i) is stated with λ^{n−|S|}, which is weaker than eq:horizon's √(1−1/K)·λ^{n−|S|}. This matches eq:credit-degree, so it is fine, but do not 'strengthen' it in the surface.
statementRisks.check: Statement matches eq:credit-degree (body.tex:178) and lem:target-contraction's second display.

statementRisks.risk: z^{[0]} must be the composed ζ = 0 network, not frozen ζ = 1 block-1 residuals.
statementRisks.check: `logits T A 0 θ` uses `block 0 θ 1 (block 0 θ 0 …)`, so ζ enters both blocks. The mixed-difference bound in step 6 relies on exactly this.

capstone.statement: Already assembled in Trace/Model/Theorem.lean as ⟨@unseen_letters_contraction hprior, @unseen_letters_score_credit hprior, @unseen_letters_outcome_credit hprior⟩. Discharging it means replacing the three surface `sorry`s with the proof-side owners Trace.Proof.unseenLettersContraction, Trace.Proof.unseenLettersScoreCredit and Trace.Proof.unseenLettersOutcomeCredit.

couplingLemma.name: Trace.Proof.relu_eq_mask_on_doubledBall
couplingLemma.statement: ∀ θ' ∈ closedBall (ε • θt) (2 * min (1/8) (cemb/4) * ε), ∀ w ζ l i m, max ((θ'.wIn l *ᵥ a_i) m + θ'.bIn l m) 0 = if 0 < θt.bIn l m then (θ'.wIn l *ᵥ a_i) m + θ'.bIn l m else 0, where a_i is the post-attention residual of block l in the ζ-network at θ' (given 0 < ε ≤ c₀ min 1 (1/Nb) and InitHyp).
couplingLemma.why: This connects the real network, with its non-smooth ReLU, to the affine-MLP network that both the paper and the locality analysis reason about. It also supplies DifferentiableAt. It holds on the doubled ball, so it covers the neighbourhood ball(θ, r₀ε) used by norm_fderiv_le_of_lip'.

crux.name: Horizon bound via Parseval on ZMod K
crux.statement: For every S and w: ‖Ĝ(w)‖₂ ≤ mixrate K p ^ (n − |S|), where Ĝ(w) = Σ_v letterWeight v • targetSignal(merge S w v). Equivalently Σ_a (P(s_n = a | w_S) − 1/K)² = (1/K)Σ_{j≠0}|ρ_j|^{2(n−|S|)} ≤ λ^{2(n−|S|)}.
crux.whyItIsTheCrux: All of part (i) and, through the credit lemma, every λ^n factor in part (ii) rest on it. It is the only place Fourier analysis, characters of ZMod K and the cos comparison |ρ_j| ≤ |ρ_1| are needed. Everything else is real inequalities.
crux.attackPlan: (1) Grep Mathlib for a ZMod.dft Parseval or a `sum_mulShift`-type orthogonality. (2) Prove `parseval_zmod` (≈30 lines) from AddChar.sum_mulShift with ZMod.isPrimitive_stdAddChar. (3) Compute the transform of Ĝ by Fintype.prod_sum (step 1b). (4) Prove |ρ_j| ≤ λ by expanding normSq and Real.cos_le_cos_of_nonneg_of_le_pi. Sanity check: mixrate 2 p = |1 − 2p| (appendix.tex:253). Before step (2), spend 10 minutes checking Arlib.MarkovChains for a lazy cycle-walk spectral gap; no declaration name is known, so do not plan on it.

crux.name: Locality-norm calculus with a width- and n-uniform softmax lemma
crux.statement: locNorm κ is a seminorm on letter functions, ≥ the sup norm, submultiplicative under bounded bilinear maps (κ ≤ 1), with locNorm(e^f − 1) ≤ e^{locNorm f} − 1, locNorm((1+β)⁻¹ − 1) ≤ N/(1−N), and Σ_{j∈V} locNorm(softmax_V(ψ)_j − 1/|V|) ≤ 8 max_j locNorm ψ_j when that max is ≤ 1/4. A two-point version of each holds as well.
crux.whyItIsTheCrux: This is what makes the paper's term enumeration ('reads ≤ 2k+1 letters, costs ε^{2+4k}') into algebra. Without the |V|-uniform softmax lemma, constants pick up n through the averaging attention.
crux.attackPlan: Group decompositions by support set (T : Finset (Fin n) → …). Prove the bilinear bound by regrouping over S ∪ S'. Prove exp via Finset.prod_add (no series). Prove the inverse via the Neumann series and locNorm ≤ κ^{-n}·sup to pass to the limit. Write softmax − 1/|V| = (α_j − β)/(|V|(1+β)) with α_j = e^{ψ_j} − 1 and β = mean α. Test the bilinear lemma on two single-letter functions first.

crux.name: Network propagation: value, ζ-difference, θ-difference and mixed bounds
crux.statement: For θ, θ' in the doubled ball, κ ∈ (0,1] and ε² ≤ cκ: locNorm κ of the logit differences satisfies (a) θ-difference at ζ = 0: ≤ Cρ(ε² + ε³κ^{-1}); (b) mixed θ/ζ difference: ≤ Cρε⁷κ^{-3}. Here ρ = ‖θ'−θ‖/ε and C depends only on a0, K, nH.
crux.whyItIsTheCrux: This is where all the ε powers and the uniformity in n, widths, alphabet, masks and Nb are earned. It is the largest body of work, about 16 layer lemmas.
crux.attackPlan: Fix the order: parameter bounds → embed → block-1 scores → block-1 weights (softmax lemma) → block-1 attention output → block-1 MLP (affine via the pattern lemma; the bias part uses εNb ≤ c₀) → block-2 scores (on block-1 outputs) → block-2 weights → block-2 output → readout. Track separate bounds for the answer position n+3, which has no κ^{-1} on its own token. Use that ω(ζ=0) = 1/|vis| does not depend on θ. Land the value bounds first (they also give the sup bounds at κ = 1), then θ-differences, then ζ-differences, then mixed.

invariants.name: Euclidean residual norms
invariants.statement: Every residual or hidden vector is measured in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (`WithLp.toLp 2`), never with the Pi sup norm of `Fin d → ℝ`.
invariants.why: Trace.opNorm and InitHyp are Euclidean. Mixing in sup norms introduces √dres or √dmlp factors and breaks width-uniformity of the constants.

invariants.name: Constants depend only on (a0, K, nH)
invariants.statement: a₁ := max a0 0 + 1/4, and every C, c, c₀ is an explicit expression in a₁, nH and √K. cemb enters only through r₀ ≤ 1/8.
invariants.why: Surface quantifier order. Any dependence on n, widths, |Sym|, p, Nb or masks makes the existential false to its spec.

invariants.name: Doubled-ball pattern
invariants.statement: On closedBall(εθ̃, 2r₀ε) (2r₀ ≤ 1/4): |bIn l m| ≥ 3ε/4, sign bIn l m = sign θ̃.bIn l m, and every MLP pre-activation for every w and every real ζ has the sign of θ̃.bIn l m.
invariants.why: Makes the MLPs affine with a fixed mask D_l = diag[0 < θ̃.bIn l m], which is independent of θ', w and ζ. Both the two-point algebra and DifferentiableAt depend on it.

invariants.name: Convex attention weights
invariants.statement: For every real ζ, attnWeight ζ θ l h x i · is nonnegative on vis(l,h,i) and sums to 1 there. At ζ = 0 it equals 1/|vis(l,h,i)|.
invariants.why: Gives ζ-independent sup bounds for the pattern lemma, and θ-independence of ω(0) for the mixed difference.

invariants.name: 0 < λ ≤ 1 and κ = λ
invariants.statement: mixrate ≤ 1 always. Under the part-(ii) hypotheses, λ > 0. The locality weight used in the credit lemma is exactly κ = λ.
invariants.why: Submultiplicativity needs κ ≤ 1, λ^{n−|S|} = λ^n λ^{-|S|} needs λ > 0, and zpow manipulations need λ ≠ 0.

invariants.name: Start count and query fixed
invariants.statement: Task.Ex sums over the letters w only. s0 and wstar are constants of the prompt.
invariants.why: Positions 0, 1, n+2, n+3 contribute weight κ^0. Only letter positions carry κ^{-1}.

modelingDecisions.decision: Prove part (ii) with a locality-weighted norm N_κ (weight κ^{-|S|} for a term reading letters S), not with the paper's ζ-Taylor expansion and term enumeration (prop:score-degree).
modelingDecisions.alternative: Formalize eq:score-split: Taylor coefficients J^{[k]}, a decomposition into T_{k,ν} each reading ≤ 2k+1 letters, the remainder J_rem with k₀ = ⌈(n−1)/2⌉, then lem:score-sum's geometric summation.
modelingDecisions.why: The paper's route needs explicit k-th ζ-derivatives of a two-block softmax network, combinatorial support counting and a Taylor remainder. N_κ gets the same bounds (score ε⁴κ^{-2}, value path ε²κ^{-1}) from submultiplicativity and three nonlinear lemmas (exp, inverse, softmax). The credit lemma then gives λ^n·N_λ in one line.
modelingDecisions.scopeCaveat: The formal proof does not contain prop:score-degree as a statement. If a referee wants that proposition itself formalized, it is extra work. The headline does not need it.

modelingDecisions.decision: Bound gradient norms through Lipschitz (two-point) estimates and `norm_fderiv_le_of_lip'`, never by computing fderiv of the network.
modelingDecisions.alternative: Track jets (value, directional derivative) through the network using HasFDerivAt chain rules, or complexify along a direction and use the Cauchy estimate (Complex.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le).
modelingDecisions.why: Exact differences obey an exact Leibniz rule, ab' − ab = (a'−a)b' + a(b'−b), so no limits, chain rules or complex copies of the network are needed. Calculus is confined to the DifferentiableAt conjuncts, which follow from the pattern lemma and fun_prop.

modelingDecisions.decision: Group locality decompositions by support set: T : Finset (Fin n) → ((Fin n → Sym) → E).
modelingDecisions.alternative: Decompositions indexed by an arbitrary Fintype ι.
modelingDecisions.why: Avoids universe and iInf problems over types, makes products a single regrouping over S ∪ S', and loses nothing, since a sum of DependsOn-S functions is DependsOn S and its sup is at most the sum of sups.

modelingDecisions.decision: Use the ReLU-free network only through a pointwise rewriting lemma (pattern lemma), not as a second forward-pass definition.
modelingDecisions.alternative: Define a proof-side `logitsLin` with fixed masks and prove logits = logitsLin on the doubled ball.
modelingDecisions.why: Fewer definitions to keep in sync. If DifferentiableAt is easier against a max-free expression, define `logitsLin` proof-side; it never enters Model/.

modelingDecisions.decision: Prove (ii-b) by splitting off the score functional and reusing the (ii-a) owner.
modelingDecisions.alternative: A separate full analysis of z_θ.
modelingDecisions.why: Only the ζ = 0 θ-difference bound is new, and it is a subset of the step-6 lemmas. This matches the paper's 'adding the zero-order term' in lem:score-sum.

modelingDecisions.decision: Characters of ZMod K via Mathlib's ZMod.stdAddChar, plus a hand-proved Parseval if none exists.
modelingDecisions.alternative: Hand-rolled exp(2πi·a.val·j/K) with explicit mod-K arithmetic, or a real Wirtinger inequality on the cycle.
modelingDecisions.why: Additivity mod K comes for free (AddChar.map_add_eq_mul). Orthogonality comes from AddChar.sum_mulShift.

files.contents:
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt
import Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Defs

/-!
# Counting modulo `K`, the two-block Transformer, and its outcome credit

The vocabulary of `thm:main` (Paper/body.tex:191-199) and the quantities it bounds.

## Encodings chosen, and why

* **Finite alphabet, expectation as a finite weighted sum.** The paper never says the
  alphabet is finite; learned token embeddings presuppose it, so `Sym` carries
  `[Fintype Sym]`. The letter law is `n` i.i.d. draws from `μ : PMF Sym`, and
  `Task.Ex f = ∑ w, (∏ t, μ (w t)) • f w`. This fills a gap the paper leaves implicit,
  and it is exactly what makes the paper's "square-integrable" hypothesis in part (i)
  automatic, which is why part (i) is stated without it. Independence of the letters
  — the whole of `lem:target-contraction` — is the product form of `Task.letterWeight`,
  so the conditioning argument is a Fubini split of a finite sum over `S` and `Sᶜ`.
* **Start count and query are fixed.** `Task.s0` and `Task.wstar` are plain fields,
  and `Task.Ex` sums over the letters `w` only. This fixedness is load-bearing for the
  independence step of `lem:target-contraction` (Paper/body.tex:163, appendix.tex:227)
  and must not change in later refactors.
* **"Depends only on the letters in `S`"** is Mathlib's `DependsOn H ↑S`; on a finite
  product space this is `σ(w_t : t ∈ S)`-measurability.
* **Parameters** form a `EuclideanSpace ℝ ParamIdx`, so `‖θ‖` is the Euclidean norm of
  the vectorised parameters (Frobenius on each block), as rem:norms
  (Paper/appendix.tex:76-81) requires. The relative position bias `β` is fixed at `0`
  for `thm:main` and excluded from `θ` and from every gradient; it is therefore simply
  absent here. Parameters at positions past the answer position and readout rows of
  non-value tokens never reach the answer logits, so they are omitted too.
* **The forward pass** is transcribed from the display at Paper/appendix.tex:95-96, not
  from a free reading of ass:arch: per head `W_Q, W_K ∈ ℝ^{d_h×d_res}` and a single
  `W_V ∈ ℝ^{d_res×d_res}` with no separate output projection, scores scaled by
  `1/√d_h`, a residual ReLU MLP `W_out ReLU(W_in h + b_in)` with no output bias, no
  LayerNorm, and a linear readout. This specific formula is the one whose power
  counting `prop:score-degree` performs.
* **The score scale `ζ`** is an explicit real argument of `logits`. It multiplies every
  attention score in *both* blocks of one composed forward pass, so block 2 reads the
  residual stream of the `ζ`-scaled block 1 (Paper/appendix.tex:298-306,
  direct_proofs/conditional_outcome.tex:29). `z_θ = logits … 1 θ` and
  `z^{[0]}_θ = logits … 0 θ`. Having `ζ` as a real variable is what lets the
  `ζ`-Taylor expansion `eq:score-split` be taken literally.
* **Submasks.** Each `(block, head, position)` has a fixed visible set; `Arch` demands
  it be causal and nonempty. Nonemptiness is what makes every softmax denominator a
  nonempty sum of exponentials, hence positive: an `Arch` with an empty mask cannot be
  built, so no instance of the theorem silently uses Lean's `x / 0 = 0`. Ordinary
  attention is the full prefix.
* **Credits are gradient norms.** `outcomeCredit` and `scoreCredit` are operator norms of
  Mathlib `fderiv`s of the credit functionals; on a Euclidean parameter space this is
  the Euclidean norm of the gradient `E[Jᵀ(y − u)]`. Because `fderiv` is `0` where a
  map is not differentiable, the theorem also asserts `DifferentiableAt`.
-/

universe u v

namespace Trace

open Matrix

/-! ## Vocabulary -/

/-- **The counting task** (def:task, Paper/body.tex:78; ass:task, appendix.tex:55): states
`ZMod K`, a finite alphabet `Sym` with letter law `μ`, the query letter `w⋆`, and the start
count `s₀`. The query and the start count are fixed, not random. -/
structure Task (K : ℕ) (Sym : Type u) where
  /-- The law of one letter; the `n` letters are i.i.d. from it. -/
  μ : PMF Sym
  /-- The query letter `w⋆`. -/
  wstar : Sym
  /-- The start count `s₀`, fixed. -/
  s0 : ZMod K

namespace Task

variable {K : ℕ} {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym) {n : ℕ}

/-- `p = μ(w⋆)`, the probability that a letter is the query. -/
noncomputable def p : ℝ := (T.μ T.wstar).toReal

/-- The answer `s_n = s₀ + ∑_t b_t (mod K)`, with `b_t = 1[w_t = w⋆]`. -/
def answer (w : Fin n → Sym) : ZMod K :=
  T.s0 + ∑ t, if w t = T.wstar then 1 else 0

/-- Probability of the letter sequence `w` under `n` i.i.d. draws from `μ`. -/
noncomputable def letterWeight (w : Fin n → Sym) : ℝ :=
  ∏ t, (T.μ (w t)).toReal

/-- Expectation over the letters only (start count and query fixed). -/
noncomputable def Ex {E : Type v} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    (f : (Fin n → Sym) → E) : E :=
  ∑ w, T.letterWeight w • f w

/-- The outcome signal `G = y − u`: the one-hot answer `y = e_{s_n}` minus the uniform
vector `u = K⁻¹ 𝟙`. -/
noncomputable def targetSignal (w : Fin n → Sym) : ZMod K → ℝ :=
  fun a => (if a = T.answer w then 1 else 0) - 1 / (K : ℝ)

/-- `‖H‖_{L²} = (E‖H‖_F²)^{1/2}` for a feature `H` with `K` rows (lem:target-contraction). -/
noncomputable def l2Norm [NeZero K] {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    (H : (Fin n → Sym) → Matrix (ZMod K) ι ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (T.Ex fun w => ∑ a, ∑ i, H w a i ^ 2)

end Task

/-- **The contraction coefficient** `λ = |1 − p + p e^{2πi/K}|` (def:lambda,
Paper/body.tex:89). The paper's other form `max_{1≤j<K} |1 − p + p e^{2πij/K}|` is a
proof obligation, not a definition. -/
noncomputable def mixrate (K : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ‖(1 - p : ℂ) + p * Complex.exp (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I / K)‖

/-- The vocabulary: letters, value tokens `ZMod K`, and the three specials
`SEP = 0`, `":" = 1`, `EOS = 2`. -/
abbrev Token (Sym : Type u) (K : ℕ) := Sym ⊕ ZMod K ⊕ Fin 3

/-- The token of letter `a`. -/
def Token.letter {Sym : Type u} {K : ℕ} (a : Sym) : Token Sym K := Sum.inl a

/-- The token of count value `v`. -/
def Token.value {Sym : Type u} {K : ℕ} (v : ZMod K) : Token Sym K := Sum.inr (Sum.inl v)

/-- The separator `SEP`. -/
def Token.sep {Sym : Type u} {K : ℕ} : Token Sym K := Sum.inr (Sum.inr 0)

/-- The answer marker `":"`. -/
def Token.colon {Sym : Type u} {K : ℕ} : Token Sym K := Sum.inr (Sum.inr 1)

/-- **The outcome prompt** (Paper/appendix.tex:107-115), positions `0, …, n+3`:
`s₀@0, w⋆@1, w_t@(1+t), SEP@(n+2), ":"@(n+3)`. Position `n+3` predicts `s_n`. Only the
letter positions depend on `w`. -/
def Task.outcomePrompt {K : ℕ} {Sym : Type u} (T : Task K Sym) {n : ℕ}
    (w : Fin n → Sym) (i : Fin (n + 4)) : Token Sym K :=
  if i.val = 0 then Token.value T.s0
  else if i.val = 1 then Token.letter T.wstar
  else if h : i.val - 2 < n then Token.letter (w ⟨i.val - 2, h⟩)
  else if i.val = n + 2 then Token.sep
  else Token.colon

/-- **Architecture shape** (ass:arch, Paper/appendix.tex:34-41): `nH` heads in each of the two
blocks, residual width `dres`, head width `dh`, MLP width `dmlp`, and for each block, head and
position a fixed causal visible set (the full prefix for ordinary attention). Sequences have
the `n + 4` positions of the outcome prompt. -/
structure Arch (nH n : ℕ) where
  /-- Residual width `d_res`. -/
  dres : ℕ
  /-- Head width `d_h`. -/
  dh : ℕ
  /-- MLP width `w`. -/
  dmlp : ℕ
  /-- The positions head `h` of block `l` attends to from position `i`. -/
  vis : Fin 2 → Fin nH → Fin (n + 4) → Finset (Fin (n + 4))
  /-- Masks are causal. -/
  vis_causal : ∀ l h i, ∀ j ∈ vis l h i, j ≤ i
  /-- Masks are nonempty, so every softmax denominator is a nonempty sum of exponentials. -/
  vis_nonempty : ∀ l h i, (vis l h i).Nonempty

/-- Index of one scalar parameter, block by block:
token embedding `E_tok` (`d_res × vocabulary`), position embedding `E_pos` (`d_res × (n+4)`),
per block and head `W_Q`, `W_K` (`d_h × d_res`) and `W_V` (`d_res × d_res`), per block
`W_in` (`w × d_res`), `b_in` (`w`) and `W_out` (`d_res × w`), and the readout `V`
(`K × d_res`, the value-token rows). The relative bias `β` is not a parameter here. -/
abbrev ParamIdx (Sym : Type u) (K : ℕ) {nH n : ℕ} (A : Arch nH n) :=
  (Fin A.dres × Token Sym K)
  ⊕ (Fin A.dres × Fin (n + 4))
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin nH × Fin A.dh × Fin A.dres)
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin nH × Fin A.dh × Fin A.dres)
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin nH × Fin A.dres × Fin A.dres)
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin A.dmlp × Fin A.dres)
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin A.dmlp)
  ⊕ (Fin 2 × Fin A.dres × Fin A.dmlp)
  ⊕ (ZMod K × Fin A.dres)

/-- **Parameters** `θ` (all but the relative bias), with the Euclidean norm of the
vectorisation (rem:norms). -/
abbrev Params (Sym : Type u) (K : ℕ) {nH n : ℕ} (A : Arch nH n) :=
  EuclideanSpace ℝ (ParamIdx Sym K A)

namespace Params

variable {Sym : Type u} {K nH n : ℕ} {A : Arch nH n} (θ : Params Sym K A)

/-- Token embedding `E_tok`, one column per token. -/
def tokEmb : Matrix (Fin A.dres) (Token Sym K) ℝ :=
  fun d v => θ (Sum.inl (d, v))

/-- Position embedding `E_pos`, one column per position. -/
def posEmb : Matrix (Fin A.dres) (Fin (n + 4)) ℝ :=
  fun d i => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (d, i)))

/-- Query matrix `W_Q` of head `h` in block `l`. -/
def wQ (l : Fin 2) (h : Fin nH) : Matrix (Fin A.dh) (Fin A.dres) ℝ :=
  fun a b => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, h, a, b))))

/-- Key matrix `W_K` of head `h` in block `l`. -/
def wK (l : Fin 2) (h : Fin nH) : Matrix (Fin A.dh) (Fin A.dres) ℝ :=
  fun a b => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, h, a, b)))))

/-- Value matrix `W_V` of head `h` in block `l` (there is no separate output projection). -/
def wV (l : Fin 2) (h : Fin nH) : Matrix (Fin A.dres) (Fin A.dres) ℝ :=
  fun a b => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, h, a, b))))))

/-- MLP input matrix `W_in` of block `l`. -/
def wIn (l : Fin 2) : Matrix (Fin A.dmlp) (Fin A.dres) ℝ :=
  fun m d => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, m, d)))))))

/-- MLP bias `b_in` of block `l`. -/
def bIn (l : Fin 2) : Fin A.dmlp → ℝ :=
  fun m => θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, m))))))))

/-- MLP output matrix `W_out` of block `l` (there is no output bias). -/
def wOut (l : Fin 2) : Matrix (Fin A.dres) (Fin A.dmlp) ℝ :=
  fun d m =>
    θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inl (l, d, m)))))))))

/-- Readout `V`: the value-token (state) rows. -/
def readout : Matrix (ZMod K) (Fin A.dres) ℝ :=
  fun v d =>
    θ (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (Sum.inr (v, d)))))))))

/-- The value-token embeddings `E_val`, the columns of `E_tok` at the `K` value tokens. -/
def valueEmb : Matrix (Fin A.dres) (ZMod K) ℝ :=
  fun d v => θ.tokEmb d (Token.value v)

end Params

section Forward

variable {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] {K nH n : ℕ} [NeZero K]

/-- Input residual stream `x_i = E_tok(token_i) + E_pos(i)` of the outcome prompt. -/
def embed (T : Task K Sym) {A : Arch nH n} (θ : Params Sym K A) (w : Fin n → Sym) :
    Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ :=
  fun i d => θ.tokEmb d (T.outcomePrompt w i) + θ.posEmb d i

/-- Attention score `ψ_{ij} = (1/√d_h) ⟨W_Q x_i, W_K x_j⟩` of head `h` in block `l`. -/
noncomputable def score {A : Arch nH n} (θ : Params Sym K A) (l : Fin 2) (h : Fin nH)
    (x : Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ) (i j : Fin (n + 4)) : ℝ :=
  (Real.sqrt A.dh)⁻¹ * ((θ.wQ l h *ᵥ x i) ⬝ᵥ (θ.wK l h *ᵥ x j))

/-- Attention weight `ω_{ij} = softmax_{j ∈ vis(i)}(ζ ψ_{ij})`, with every score scaled by `ζ`.
The denominator runs over the visible set `A.vis l h i`, nonempty by `Arch.vis_nonempty`. -/
noncomputable def attnWeight {A : Arch nH n} (ζ : ℝ) (θ : Params Sym K A) (l : Fin 2)
    (h : Fin nH) (x : Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ) (i j : Fin (n + 4)) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (ζ * score θ l h x i j) / ∑ k ∈ A.vis l h i, Real.exp (ζ * score θ l h x i k)

/-- One Transformer block `l` with score scale `ζ` (Paper/appendix.tex:95-96):
`a_i = x_i + ∑_h ∑_{j ∈ vis(i)} ω_{ij} W_V x_j`, then `a_i + W_out ReLU(W_in a_i + b_in)`. -/
noncomputable def block {A : Arch nH n} (ζ : ℝ) (θ : Params Sym K A) (l : Fin 2)
    (x : Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ) : Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ :=
  let a : Fin (n + 4) → Fin A.dres → ℝ := fun i =>
    x i + ∑ h, ∑ j ∈ A.vis l h i, attnWeight ζ θ l h x i j • (θ.wV l h *ᵥ x j)
  fun i => a i + θ.wOut l *ᵥ fun m => max ((θ.wIn l *ᵥ a i) m + θ.bIn l m) 0

/-- **State logits at the answer position** `n + 3` of the outcome prompt, for the network
whose attention scores are all scaled by `ζ` in both blocks of one composed forward pass.
`z_θ = logits T A 1 θ`; `z^{[0]}_θ = logits T A 0 θ` (uniform attention over each visible set,
composed through both blocks). -/
noncomputable def logits (T : Task K Sym) (A : Arch nH n) (ζ : ℝ) (θ : Params Sym K A)
    (w : Fin n → Sym) : ZMod K → ℝ :=
  θ.readout *ᵥ block ζ θ 1 (block ζ θ 0 (embed T θ w)) (Fin.last (n + 3))

end Forward

/-- The `ℓ²` operator norm of a real matrix, `‖M‖ = sup_{‖x‖ ≤ 1} ‖M x‖`
(definitionally Mathlib's `Matrix.l2_opNorm_def` under `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`). -/
noncomputable def opNorm {m k : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
    (M : Matrix m k ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Matrix.toEuclideanLin M)‖

/-- **Assumption A2 on the unscaled initialisation `θ̃`** (ass:init, Paper/appendix.tex:43-52):
every weight matrix and embedding block has operator norm at most `a0`; the value-token
embeddings have smallest singular value at least `cemb` (`‖E_val x‖ ≥ cemb ‖x‖`); every MLP bias
coordinate has `|b̃_m| ≥ 1` and every MLP bias vector has norm at most `Nb`. -/
structure InitHyp {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] {K nH n : ℕ} [NeZero K]
    {A : Arch nH n} (θt : Params Sym K A) (a0 cemb Nb : ℝ) : Prop where
  tokEmb_le : opNorm θt.tokEmb ≤ a0
  posEmb_le : opNorm θt.posEmb ≤ a0
  wQ_le : ∀ l h, opNorm (θt.wQ l h) ≤ a0
  wK_le : ∀ l h, opNorm (θt.wK l h) ≤ a0
  wV_le : ∀ l h, opNorm (θt.wV l h) ≤ a0
  wIn_le : ∀ l, opNorm (θt.wIn l) ≤ a0
  wOut_le : ∀ l, opNorm (θt.wOut l) ≤ a0
  readout_le : opNorm θt.readout ≤ a0
  valueEmb_sigmaMin : ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (ZMod K),
    cemb * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin θt.valueEmb x‖
  bIn_ge_one : ∀ l m, 1 ≤ |θt.bIn l m|
  bIn_norm_le : ∀ l, ‖(WithLp.toLp 2 (θt.bIn l) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin A.dmlp))‖ ≤ Nb

/-- **The ball `B_ε`** around `θ₀ = ε θ̃`, of radius `r₀ ε` with `r₀ = min(1/8, cemb/4)`
(ass:init); `β = 0` is built in because `β` is not a parameter. -/
def initBall {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] {K nH n : ℕ} [NeZero K] {A : Arch nH n}
    (θt : Params Sym K A)
    (ε cemb : ℝ) : Set (Params Sym K A) :=
  Metric.closedBall (ε • θt) (min (1 / 8) (cemb / 4) * ε)

/-! ## The quantity -/

section Quantity

variable {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] {K nH n : ℕ} [NeZero K]

/-- **Credit of a feature** `H` with `K` rows: `‖E[Hᵀ(y − u)]‖`, the Euclidean norm
(the left side of eq:credit-degree, Paper/body.tex:178). -/
noncomputable def featureCredit (T : Task K Sym) {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    (H : (Fin n → Sym) → Matrix (ZMod K) ι ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ‖(WithLp.toLp 2 (T.Ex fun w => (H w)ᵀ *ᵥ T.targetSignal w) : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)‖

/-- The outcome credit functional `Φ_out(θ) = E⟨z_θ, y − u⟩` (def:credit, def:losses). -/
noncomputable def outcomeFunctional (T : Task K Sym) (A : Arch nH n)
    (θ : Params Sym K A) : ℝ :=
  T.Ex fun w => logits T A 1 θ w ⬝ᵥ T.targetSignal w

/-- The score-mediated credit functional `E⟨z_θ − z^{[0]}_θ, y − u⟩`, whose gradient is
`E[J_scoreᵀ(y − u)]` with `J_score = J_z − J^{[0]}` (Paper/appendix.tex:26-30). -/
noncomputable def scoreFunctional (T : Task K Sym) (A : Arch nH n)
    (θ : Params Sym K A) : ℝ :=
  T.Ex fun w => (logits T A 1 θ w - logits T A 0 θ w) ⬝ᵥ T.targetSignal w

/-- **Outcome credit** `‖∇_θ Φ_out(θ)‖ = ‖E[J_zᵀ(y − u)]‖`. -/
noncomputable def outcomeCredit (T : Task K Sym) (A : Arch nH n) (θ : Params Sym K A) : ℝ :=
  ‖fderiv ℝ (outcomeFunctional T A) θ‖

/-- **Score-mediated credit** `‖E[J_scoreᵀ(y − u)]‖`. -/
noncomputable def scoreCredit (T : Task K Sym) (A : Arch nH n) (θ : Params Sym K A) : ℝ :=
  ‖fderiv ℝ (scoreFunctional T A) θ‖

end Quantity

end Trace

files.contents:
import Trace.Model.Prelude
import Trace.Model.Prior
import Trace.Meta.ModelClosure
import Mathlib.Logic.Function.DependsOn
import Trace.Analysis.Contraction
import Trace.Analysis.ScoreCredit
import Trace.Analysis.OutcomeCredit

/-!
# Unseen letters erase outcome credit (`thm:main`, Paper/body.tex:191-199)

Under ass:arch, ass:init and ass:task, with the start count and the query fixed:

* **(i)** for every set `S` of letters and every `H` that depends only on the letters in
  `S`, `‖E[Hᵀ(y − u)]‖ ≤ λ^{n−|S|} ‖H‖_{L²}`
  (`unseen_letters_contraction`);
* **(ii)** for every `n ≥ 2` and `θ ∈ B_ε`: if `ε² ≤ cλ`, the score-mediated credit is at most
  `C ε⁶ λ^{n−3}` (`unseen_letters_score_credit`); if `ε ≤ cλ`, the whole outcome credit is at
  most `C ε λ^n` (`unseen_letters_outcome_credit`).

Departures from the literal text, each one a repair rather than a weakening:

* `0 < ε` is a hypothesis of (ii). `thm:main` omits it, but `lem:score-sum`, which its proof
  invokes, assumes it; at `ε = 0` the point `θ₀ = 0` has every MLP pre-activation exactly `0`,
  where ReLU is not differentiable, and `λ^{n−3}` at `n = 2` needs `λ > 0`, which `ε > 0` and
  `ε² ≤ cλ` supply.
* `λ^{n−3}` is an integer power `mixrate K T.p ^ ((n : ℤ) - 3)`. Natural subtraction would turn
  it into `λ⁰ = 1` at `n = 2, 3`, a different claim.
* `DifferentiableAt` is asserted alongside each credit bound, so that a bound on
  Mathlib's `fderiv` (which is `0` off the differentiable locus) cannot hold vacuously.
* The paper's "square-integrable" hypothesis in (i) is dropped: the alphabet is finite,
  so every `H` is square-integrable.

Constants. `c₀` (the threshold `ε₀ = c₀ min(1, 1/N_b)` of ass:init), `c` and `C` are chosen
after `a0`, `cemb`, `K` and the number of heads `nH` only, and before `n`, the widths, the masks,
the alphabet, `μ`, `p`, `s₀`, `w⋆`, `N_b`, `θ̃`, `ε` and `θ` (Paper/appendix.tex:60-61, 227).
(ii-a) and (ii-b) each carry their own constants; taking `c₀, c` to be the minima and `C` the
maximum of the two triples gives one triple serving both, since shrinking `c₀`, `c` and growing
`C` only weakens each hypothesis-conclusion pair, so the split loses nothing.
-/

universe u v

namespace Trace

open Matrix

/-- **Part (i): conditional contraction** (eq:credit-degree; lem:target-contraction,
Paper/appendix.tex:264-290). A feature that reads only the letters in `S` has credit at most
`λ^{n−|S|}` times its `L²` norm. Architecture-free. -/
theorem unseen_letters_contraction (hprior : Prior)
    {K : ℕ} [NeZero K] (hK : 2 ≤ K)
    {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym)
    (hp0 : 0 < T.p) (hp1 : T.p < 1)
    (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    (H : (Fin n → Sym) → Matrix (ZMod K) ι ℝ) (hH : DependsOn H (S : Set (Fin n))) :
    featureCredit T H ≤ mixrate K T.p ^ (n - S.card) * T.l2Norm H := by
    exact Trace.Proof.unseenLettersContraction hprior (K := K) hK (Sym := Sym) T hp0 hp1 n S (ι := ι) H hH

/-- **Part (ii-a): score-mediated credit** (lem:score-sum, Paper/appendix.tex:494-499). -/
theorem unseen_letters_score_credit (hprior : Prior)
    (a0 cemb : ℝ) (hcemb : 0 < cemb) (K : ℕ) [NeZero K] (hK : 2 ≤ K) (nH : ℕ) :
    ∃ c₀ c C : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      ∀ (Sym : Type u) [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym),
        0 < T.p → T.p < 1 →
      ∀ (A : Arch nH n) (θt : Params Sym K A) (Nb : ℝ), InitHyp θt a0 cemb Nb →
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ c₀ * min 1 (1 / Nb) →
      ∀ θ ∈ initBall θt ε cemb,
        ε ^ 2 ≤ c * mixrate K T.p →
          DifferentiableAt ℝ (scoreFunctional T A) θ ∧
            scoreCredit T A θ ≤ C * ε ^ 6 * mixrate K T.p ^ ((n : ℤ) - 3) := by
    exact Trace.Proof.unseenLettersScoreCredit hprior a0 cemb hcemb K hK nH

/-- **Part (ii-b): outcome credit** (eq:thm1-full, Paper/appendix.tex:502-505). -/
theorem unseen_letters_outcome_credit (hprior : Prior)
    (a0 cemb : ℝ) (hcemb : 0 < cemb) (K : ℕ) [NeZero K] (hK : 2 ≤ K) (nH : ℕ) :
    ∃ c₀ c C : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      ∀ (Sym : Type u) [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym),
        0 < T.p → T.p < 1 →
      ∀ (A : Arch nH n) (θt : Params Sym K A) (Nb : ℝ), InitHyp θt a0 cemb Nb →
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ c₀ * min 1 (1 / Nb) →
      ∀ θ ∈ initBall θt ε cemb,
        ε ≤ c * mixrate K T.p →
          DifferentiableAt ℝ (outcomeFunctional T A) θ ∧
            outcomeCredit T A θ ≤ C * ε * mixrate K T.p ^ n := by
    exact Trace.Proof.unseenLettersOutcomeCredit hprior a0 cemb hcemb K hK nH

/-- **Unseen letters erase outcome credit** (`thm:main`): parts (i), (ii-a) and (ii-b). -/
theorem unseen_letters_erase_outcome_credit (hprior : Prior) :
    (∀ {K : ℕ} [NeZero K], 2 ≤ K →
      ∀ {Sym : Type u} [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym),
        0 < T.p → T.p < 1 →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin n)) {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]
        (H : (Fin n → Sym) → Matrix (ZMod K) ι ℝ), DependsOn H (S : Set (Fin n)) →
        featureCredit T H ≤ mixrate K T.p ^ (n - S.card) * T.l2Norm H) ∧
    (∀ (a0 cemb : ℝ), 0 < cemb → ∀ (K : ℕ) [NeZero K], 2 ≤ K → ∀ nH : ℕ,
      ∃ c₀ c C : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
        ∀ (Sym : Type u) [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym),
          0 < T.p → T.p < 1 →
        ∀ (A : Arch nH n) (θt : Params Sym K A) (Nb : ℝ), InitHyp θt a0 cemb Nb →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ c₀ * min 1 (1 / Nb) →
        ∀ θ ∈ initBall θt ε cemb,
          ε ^ 2 ≤ c * mixrate K T.p →
            DifferentiableAt ℝ (scoreFunctional T A) θ ∧
              scoreCredit T A θ ≤ C * ε ^ 6 * mixrate K T.p ^ ((n : ℤ) - 3)) ∧
    (∀ (a0 cemb : ℝ), 0 < cemb → ∀ (K : ℕ) [NeZero K], 2 ≤ K → ∀ nH : ℕ,
      ∃ c₀ c C : ℝ, 0 < c₀ ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
        ∀ (Sym : Type u) [Fintype Sym] [DecidableEq Sym] (T : Task K Sym),
          0 < T.p → T.p < 1 →
        ∀ (A : Arch nH n) (θt : Params Sym K A) (Nb : ℝ), InitHyp θt a0 cemb Nb →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε ≤ c₀ * min 1 (1 / Nb) →
        ∀ θ ∈ initBall θt ε cemb,
          ε ≤ c * mixrate K T.p →
            DifferentiableAt ℝ (outcomeFunctional T A) θ ∧
              outcomeCredit T A θ ≤ C * ε * mixrate K T.p ^ n) :=
  ⟨@unseen_letters_contraction hprior, @unseen_letters_score_credit hprior,
    @unseen_letters_outcome_credit hprior⟩

end Trace

#modelClosureOfType Trace.unseen_letters_erase_outcome_credit
#print axioms Trace.unseen_letters_erase_outcome_credit

#surplusIn Trace.Model from Trace.unseen_letters_erase_outcome_credit

definitionOfDone: The mechanical checks pass. They are run by the extension over the whole project between rounds — the build, the `sorry` warnings, the axiom profile of every headline, a sweep for escape hatches, the closure checks, and the two layout rules — and what they find comes back to you as the next round's brief. Build the modules you created and read their errors; do not try to run the gate.
`#print axioms` on the capstone reports exactly the three ambient axioms — propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound — and nothing else.
No `declaration uses sorry` warning anywhere in the build output.
A grep sweep for `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` and `axiom` over the project comes back clean, and agrees with the other two checks.
The closure checks have been observed to *fail* on a deliberately broken control, so that their passing means something.

The audit surface still states the paper's theorem: every claim the paper makes is in it, and nothing was weakened to make a proof go through. No script decides this one — the extension's handoff check reads the paper and the surface side by side, and it runs as the last step of a run.
